Team — draft content below, pulled from our ops playbook. I'll convert this to a short (2–3 page) RFP paragraph + appendix with the artifacts and attach vendor templates. Please flag edits.

--- DRAFT: Marketplace listing and procurement summary (for RFP) ---

1) Commercial models supported
- Metered/usage-based: Supported on AWS (Marketplace Metering), limited on Azure (requires SaaS Fulfillment metering integration), GCP supports usage-based SaaS via Marketplace if packaged as SaaS.
- Subscription (recurring): Supported across AWS, Azure, and GCP via their respective SaaS/subscription offers.
- Private Offer / Negotiated Pricing: Supported on AWS (Seller Private Offers) and Azure (Private Offers via Commercial Marketplace), GCP supports negotiated terms via partner sales channels. Private offers require an executed commercial agreement or PO and registration of offer IDs.

2) Billing flow options and implications
- Provider-billed (marketplace billing): Buyer is billed via cloud provider and provider remits to Redwood. This simplifies procurement for buyers but imposes marketplace fees and payout lag.
- Vendor-billed (direct invoicing): Redwood invoices the customer directly under our standard SaaS contract; common for enterprise deals that want direct contractual relationships or special terms.
- Hybrid: Private offer + PO where contract is vendor-billed but listing is available in the marketplace for procurement traceability.

3) Typical onboarding/timeline
- Seller registration and tax/VAT forms: 1–3 business days (depends on vendor).
- Technical integration (SaaS Fulfillment registration, metering hooks): 5–10 business days for basic setup; 2–4 weeks for metered and integration testing with customer telemetry.
- Security and procurement reviews by buyer (customer timelines): often 1–4 weeks depending on customer; SOC2 evidence can accelerate approval.

4) Compliance & artifacts we can provide
- SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), ISO 27001 certificate (if applicable), DPA (standard), penetration test summary, data flow diagrams, audit log export samples.
- If additional attestation needed we can schedule a short vendor security call and provide an NDA/POC environment.

5) Technical packaging guidance
- AWS: Preferred path is SaaS (SaaS Fulfillment) for zero-ops buyer experience. AMI/EC2 images acceptable for dedicated deployments but require separate listing. Metering uses AWS Metering Service and integ points require service token exchange.
- Azure: Azure Marketplace SaaS Fulfillment supports both plan-based and meter-based billing; requires registration of SaaS fulfillment endpoint and seller ID.
- GCP: GCP Marketplace supports SaaS via marketplace SaaS offers or container-based deployment; metering and private pricing handled via partner console.

6) What we need from Procurement for Private Offers
- Signed PO referencing the private offer ID, buyer billing contact, and remit details. For vendor-billed contracts we need countersigned contract and legal contact.

7) Attachments & next steps
- Attach: aws_private_offer_template.pdf, azure_sla_note.docx, marketplace_requirements_grid.xlsx (maps ask->artifact).
- Next steps: I'll produce the short RFP blurb and an appendix with the artifacts. Lauren, please add the canonical wording for vendor-billed vs provider-billed options and confirm the turnaround for private offer setup (billing/legal checklist).

--- end draft ---

Markus
